answer: Assign every identity a different harbor — a real locale, dataset, or event its epoch work must be grounded in — and require the work to bend to that context like a willow: specific names, constraints, and trade-offs only that setting supplies. A sybil operator can mint identities cheaply but cannot fabricate dozens of distinct, locally true bodies of work; generic filler stands out against genuinely grounded peers. At the zenith of the epoch, work sharing an assigned context is compared side by side, and thin, interchangeable submissions are discarded together.
